title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Flower Market. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Flower Market
options.lineage: KR Market, Bengaluru: marigold and jasmine sold by the string
options.thesis: The portfolio as a stall of hanging strings: every project is one strand you can count, pull and open.
materials: strung flower beads as index strands
options.viewport: Her name and role set huge in green on a full marigold field, with all 12 projects hanging from the top edge as labelled strands; CV and LinkedIn sit in the top bar.
options.risk: If the strands are drawn ornamentally rather than used as the index, it tips into the 'too decorated' you ruled out.

raised.raise: The index gets fixed columns that never move (project, made for, place, year, discipline), ranked by year.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: the name at wall size, everything else small and exact, nothing in between.
One real printed piece blown to wall scale per case study, the photo treated as the print material.
Only the strand you point at lights up in full colour; the rest of the stall rests in the field colour.
Sections are full-width colour bands that move from marigold through saffron to jasmine as you scroll.

options.label: The Card Shop Sample Album
options.lineage: Avenue Road and Chickpet wedding-card shops, Bengaluru
options.thesis: The portfolio as the thick sample album a card shop hands you across the counter: tabbed, numbered, one design per page.
options.viewport: A tabbed album cover with her name and role; the tab edge is the index of all 12 projects, each tab opening its page.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: it sits closest to every wedding-stationery site, which may undersell her to employers.

options.label: The Silkscreen Poster
options.thesis: Flat, fearless colour fields around one emblem: her ABN monogram, with her name running round the edge in English, Kannada, Hindi and Tamil.
options.viewport: A centred ABN monogram on a red field, name and role in four scripts as the border; the index starts directly below.
options.case: Fuses well: the four scripts echo the many traditions in her suites. It holds audience identification but loses on clarity for employers scanning the work.
options.risk: A poster world can read as a political or campaign site if the emblem is set too large.

options.label: Split-flap Board
options.thesis: The project index as a departure board.
options.viewport: A black board listing all 12 projects in flap rows.
options.case: Fuses poorly: travel signage says nothing about stationery, and its black ground fights 'not too dark'.
options.risk: Cold and mechanical next to warm printed work.
options.kept: Fixed index columns that never move, ranked by year.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Her name as a live type specimen.
options.viewport: One giant letter with an axis slider.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it shows off a typeface, not her drawing or print work.
options.risk: Reads as a font foundry, not a designer.

options.label: Hybrid Collage
options.thesis: The portfolio as one deep layered collage.
options.case: Fuses poorly: layering competes with her own motifs, the 'too decorated' you ruled out.
options.risk: Buries the work under the collage.
options.kept: One printed piece blown to wall scale.

options.label: Night Plankton
options.thesis: Pointer trails of light on a black sea.
options.viewport: A black field that lights where you move.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark and moody, the opposite of her bright work.
options.kept: Only the active item lights; the rest rests.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: Sections as light bands from night to day.
options.viewport: A black stage with a cobalt horizon.
options.case: Fuses poorly: theatre lighting has no tie to print, and it opens dark.
options.kept: Sections as full-width colour bands that change as you scroll.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean designer portfolio: name and role, then a grid of project thumbnails, about and contact.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line role top left, CV and LinkedIn top right, a three-column grid of all 12 covers below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other portfolio by design.
